output.summary: The analysis defined the problem (PD-1) as: shipment notices from Shipper to Carrier via handoff H-1 are rejected because they fail Carrier's categorical business validation rules on location and event-sequence reference data (reason codes LOC_UNKNOWN and EVENT_ORDER), not because of content errors or carrier-side flakiness. This was established from the authoritative carrier reject-log (E-01), which showed all 3 sampled rejections split into LOC_UNKNOWN (N-1, N-2) and EVENT_ORDER (N-3) (facts F-01, F-02), yielding metrics M-CATEGORICAL-REJECT-RATE=1.0 and M-LOC-UNKNOWN-SHARE=0.667. This directly tested and rejected the operations manager's original request (claim CL-01) to blanket auto-fix and resubmit every rejected notice on the premise that the carrier system is flaky (claim CL-02, evidence E-02); hypothesis H-ERROR-IN-NOTICE-CONTENT was formally REJECTED, while H-CARRIER-RULE-MISMATCH and H-UPSTREAM-DATA-QUALITY are SUPPORTED. The DEFINE gate returned only a CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two critical unknowns (root-cause locus and sample-size adequacy) into open verification obligations (VOBs). What was released is the narrower, already-completed work: investigating the EVENT_ORDER rejects and flagging unresolved rejects for Carrier's interface owner (SH-INT) to review — not the requested auto-fix/resubmit automation. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with nothing held back, because the still-open VOBs (root-cause locus, sample-size adequacy, EVENT_ORDER cause) block only scope beyond what was actually released, notably the resubmit action, which the success criterion SC-NO-BLIND-RESUBMIT explicitly requires to stay gated behind human approval. Deeper remedies that could close the open questions — cross-checking location codes against Shipper's own reference data, and a structural cross-org data-sharing arrangement — were judged infeasible in the available time and remain unfinished.
